correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts all flipping masks via degree-two propagation; it checks endpoint conditions for zero, one or both active paths and counts stable path interiors through exact integer compositions including the one-vertex boundary. It proves the Fibonacci/six-periodic equivalence by rational generating functions. A separate direct update program exhaustively matched all three class counts for 66 legal pairs with n<=14 (327,696 states), but those finite tests are not substituted for the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Period-two boundedness is a strict general property but has no specified implication for exact values of N(n,d) beyond restricting temporal lengths; full local equations and graph-specific counting remain necessary. The fixed-ring results have fewer edges and cannot dominate the one-chord census under graph monotonicity, which is not available for majority dynamics.

evidence: An unchorded odd cycle has no primitive two-cycle because every flipping vertex forces both cycle neighbors to flip, hence impossible odd-length alternation.
For the single-chord odd cycle the explicit construction yields at least two endpoint-only and two one-arc-flipping orbits; the source models without a chord do not contain these states.
The exact class populations use constrained interior words and graph-dependent endpoint voting, absent from the cited general period-two result.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the general eventual period restriction nor unchorded-ring configuration structure logically determines the additional dynamical states created by a chord; in particular no monotonic edge-addition implication can supply the exact count. A matching formula under a renamed theta-graph presentation remains a residual historical possibility.

originality.rationale: The exact two-parameter primitive-two-cycle census and the sharp emergence of oscillations upon one chord do not follow from the known eventual period-two theorem or unchorded one-dimensional majority classification; targeted archive literature and research database comparisons did not identify a matching or stronger chorded-cycle theorem. Full historical priority cannot be certified, and one older original was inaccessible.

value.rationale: A single chord is the minimal edge perturbation of an odd cycle and changes qualitative recurrent dynamics from no primitive oscillations to at least four. The exact infinite-family count separates all mechanisms, depends nontrivially on both chord arc lengths and reduces to Fibonacci growth plus a six-periodic correction. These are natural graph-dynamical invariants, not arbitrary finite samples.
